evidence: All use cases (AssignTaskUseCase, CompleteTaskUseCase, CreateProjectUseCase, CreateTaskUseCase, CreateUserUseCase, ListTasksUseCase) take domain repository ports via constructor injection and expose execute(...)

src/application/dtos.ts declares input DTOs (CreateUserDto, CreateProjectDto, CreateTaskDto, AssignTaskDto, ListTasksDto) used by the corresponding use cases, plus TaskResponseDto/toTaskResponse output mapping
Status parsing goes through the domain's parseTaskStatus in both create-task-use-case.ts and list-tasks-use-case.ts rather than being re-implemented

create-user-use-case.ts inlines `typeof dto.name !== "string" || dto.name.trim() === ""` while create-project-use-case.ts puts the same check in assertExecuteRule; these are similar but separate per-entity rules
create-task-use-case.ts and list-tasks-use-case.ts each check projects.findById and throw NotFoundError("project not found"), which is a per-use-case precondition
parsedVerdict.reasoning:
The module is one cohesive application layer of use-case classes plus their DTOs. Every use case follows the same pattern: constructor-injected domain repository ports and IdGenerator, an execute(dto) method, a not-found check that throws domain errors, then a call to the entity and save. All the use cases rely on the shared input DTOs in dtos.ts. Status parsing goes through the domain's parseTaskStatus in both create-task and list-tasks, so that rule lives in one place. None of the files bypass the repository abstraction or reach into infrastructure.

The borderline issue is the non-empty-name check. It appears in create-user-use-case.ts (inline) and create-project-use-case.ts (in the helper assertExecuteRule). The checks are similar, but they guard two different entities, User and Project, so they are separate rules rather than one invariant copied twice. The "project not found" check in create-task and list-tasks is normal per-use-case precondition handling, not a misplaced invariant. Writing one check inline and the other as a file-local helper is a style inconsistency, not a split of concerns or a bypass of an abstraction.
